caseStudies.title: Secure Document Link Gateway
caseStudies.problem: Business applications needed time-limited, revocable access to documents stored on remote systems without routing every download through a database lookup or exposing origin URLs.
caseStudies.context: Enterprise operations platform serving generated and archived documents across internal business applications.
caseStudies.architecture: Business applications POST JSON link requests to a Link Generator API, which stores lifecycle records (ACTIVE, BLOCKED, EXPIRED) in PostgreSQL and returns AES-GCM encrypted tokens containing the document reference and expiry. Background downloaders fetch remote files into a local file store grouped by application and filename, while a stateless Link Gateway decrypts incoming tokens and streams cached documents.
challenges: Synchronising local cache availability with link expiry across multiple independent background schedulers without relying on per-request session state.
Preventing partially downloaded files from being served before background retrieval finishes.
decisions: Embedded expiry and document coordinates inside AES-GCM authenticated tokens so the serving gateway validates integrity and TTL statelessly.
Staged remote fetches before atomically moving completed files into the active local store directory.
Separated lifecycle housekeeping (15 s cadence) from expired file cleanup (60 s cadence) to isolate state transitions from disk I/O.
reliability: Stateless download verification removes database contention from the hot streaming path.
Explicit ACTIVE / BLOCKED / EXPIRED states allow link revocation and deterministic disk reclamation.
results: Verified design documented in repository: stateless token verification on downloads paired with bounded scheduled housekeeping and cleanup loops.

caseStudies.title: XML Transformation Pipeline
caseStudies.problem: Upstream enterprise systems send diverse XML payloads over AMQP that require routing, custom XSLT transformations with Java extensions, and hot-deployable rule updates without service restarts.
caseStudies.context: Asynchronous enterprise messaging middleware connecting upstream and downstream systems at Kuehne+Nagel.
caseStudies.architecture: Upstream systems publish XML messages to a RabbitMQ request queue consumed by a bounded worker pool. A Router resolves target out-queues, a Saxon XSLT transformer applies cached stylesheets backed by Java extension functions loaded from plugin jars, and transformed payloads are delivered to destination queues.
challenges: Isolating third-party/custom Java extension jars loaded at runtime so conflicting classes do not leak into the host application.
Reloading stylesheets and plugin jars on redeploy without restarting the running JVM service or dropping in-flight messages.
decisions: Loaded each extension jar via its own isolated classloader and cached compiled XSLT stylesheets for throughput.
Triggered controlled context reloads on redeploy rather than full process restarts.
Configured a bounded worker pool on the RabbitMQ consumer to apply predictable backpressure.
reliability: Dedicated error path emails failure diagnostics and requeues failed messages so transient faults do not result in silent data loss.
Classloader isolation prevents plugin dependency clashes from destabilising the core pipeline.
results: Verified design documented in repository: zero-restart context reloads for transformation plugins and explicit error-notification plus requeue guarantees.

caseStudies.title: Messenger Archive & Semantic Search
caseStudies.scope: Personal engineering project (independent of employer work)
caseStudies.problem: Long-running personal chat archives mix text and voice messages across thousands of threads, making keyword lookup ineffective for finding past discussions or feeding context to LLM agents.
caseStudies.context: Self-directed personal engineering project built outside employer work to explore Rust/Python interop, local speech-to-text, vector search, and MCP.
caseStudies.architecture: A Rust sync service pulls history via MTProto with flood-wait backoff into PostgreSQL. A Python worker claims pending voice rows using PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED and transcribes them with Whisper. A Rust indexer generates batched local embeddings and upserts points into Qdrant, exposed to LLM agents via an MCP server (stdio and HTTP).
challenges: No distributed transaction spans PostgreSQL, Qdrant, and the sync cursor checkpoint.
Respecting MTProto rate limits while recovering cleanly from crashes mid-batch.
decisions: Computed deterministic UUIDv5 Qdrant point IDs from message identity so retries overwrite idempotently instead of creating duplicates.
Advanced the PostgreSQL sync cursor only after each Qdrant upsert succeeds.
Used PostgreSQL SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for lock-free concurrent voice transcription workers.
reliability: At-least-once indexing combined with deterministic UUIDv5 upserts yields idempotent eventual consistency without 2PC.
Flood-wait backoff and bounded retries protect upstream MTProto sessions.
results: End-to-end personal archive searchable semantically across text and transcribed voice messages through standard MCP clients.

architectureDiagrams.title: Event-Driven XML Transformation Pipeline
architectureDiagrams.label: XML transformation pipeline: upstream systems, RabbitMQ request queue, router, isolated XSLT transformer, out-queues, and error recovery
architectureDiagrams.summary: Asynchronous AMQP message routing with bounded concurrency, isolated plugin classloaders, zero-restart context reloads, and non-destructive failure recovery.

nodes.title: Upstream Systems
nodes.responsibility: Publishes integration payloads as AMQP messages without coupling to downstream schemas.
nodes.tradeoffs: Async decoupling absorbs burst traffic at the cost of eventual end-to-end delivery.

nodes.title: Message Broker Queue
nodes.responsibility: Buffers incoming requests and dispatches messages to a bounded pool of Java consumers.
nodes.tradeoffs: Bounded consumer concurrency prevents OOM under spikes while bounding peak single-node throughput.

nodes.title: Message Router
nodes.responsibility: Inspects message metadata, verifies target out-queue configuration, and selects the transformation flow.
nodes.tradeoffs: Validating destination readiness early avoids wasted transformation work on misrouted payloads.

nodes.title: XSLT Transformer & Plugins
nodes.responsibility: Executes cached Saxon XSLT stylesheets invoking Java extension functions from isolated plugin jars with hot context reload.
nodes.tradeoffs: Per-plugin classloader isolation prevents library conflicts and enables hot reload, with care needed to release old classloaders cleanly.

nodes.title: Destination Queues
nodes.responsibility: Delivers canonical downstream XML payloads to target consumer queues.
nodes.tradeoffs: Downstream consumers process asynchronously and should tolerate duplicate deliveries on broker redelivery.

nodes.title: Error Notification & Requeue
nodes.responsibility: Captures transformation or routing faults, emails diagnostic context, and requeues the message so payloads are preserved.
nodes.tradeoffs: Automatic requeue prevents silent data loss, requiring monitoring/backoff to avoid tight poison-message loops.

architectureDiagrams.title: Secure Document Link Gateway
architectureDiagrams.label: Document link flow: business application, encrypted token generator, lifecycle store, background downloader, file store, and stateless gateway
architectureDiagrams.summary: AES-GCM encrypted time-limited links enabling stateless file streaming decoupled from remote document fetching and lifecycle cleanup.

nodes.title: Business Application
nodes.responsibility: Requests a shareable, time-limited download token for an existing remote document.
nodes.tradeoffs: Separating link minting from file serving keeps business apps unaware of storage mechanics.

nodes.title: Link Generator API
nodes.responsibility: Encrypts and authenticates document coordinates plus TTL using AES-GCM and records initial lifecycle state.
nodes.tradeoffs: Authenticated ciphertext prevents tampering and avoids DB reads on download, while revocation still checks lifecycle state.

nodes.title: Lifecycle Store (PostgreSQL)
nodes.responsibility: Tracks authoritative document metadata, download state, and expiration timestamps.
nodes.tradeoffs: Relational state guarantees clear transition semantics for background workers without blocking gateway reads.

nodes.title: Background Downloader
nodes.responsibility: Retrieves documents from remote storage into staging and moves complete files into the active store.
nodes.tradeoffs: Async staging prevents slow origin systems from tying up HTTP threads or exposing partial files.

nodes.title: Local File Cache
nodes.responsibility: Stores verified local copies ready for immediate byte streaming.
nodes.tradeoffs: Local disk caching reduces origin load and latency, bounded by scheduled TTL eviction.

nodes.title: Stateless Link Gateway
nodes.responsibility: Validates AES-GCM tag and token expiry, then streams the file from the local cache.
nodes.tradeoffs: Stateless token validation scales horizontally with minimal latency; instant revocation relies on housekeeping sync.

architectureDiagrams.title: Distributed Background Processing & Lifecycle Coordination
architectureDiagrams.label: Distributed background processing: lifecycle store, housekeeping scheduler, retrieval workers, cache store, and cleanup scheduler
architectureDiagrams.summary: Coordinating asynchronous retrieval, state transitions, and TTL cleanup across independent scheduled loops without distributed locks on the request path.

nodes.title: Lifecycle State Table
nodes.responsibility: Acts as the single source of truth for document availability, retry eligibility, and expiration windows.
nodes.tradeoffs: Explicit state enums simplify reasoning about concurrent jobs compared to implicit filesystem timestamps.

nodes.title: Housekeeping Scheduler (15 s)
nodes.responsibility: Periodically evaluates TTL thresholds and marks expired entries or schedules missing fetches.
nodes.tradeoffs: A 15-second tick bounds staleness cleanly without continuous polling overhead.

nodes.title: Queue / Work Claimer
nodes.responsibility: Allows concurrent workers to claim pending jobs safely without double-processing the same record.
nodes.tradeoffs: Database row-claim semantics avoid operating a separate coordinator for moderate job volumes.

nodes.title: Staged Retrieval & Atomic Publish
nodes.responsibility: Writes downloaded bytes to a temporary location and moves them into place only after full transfer.
nodes.tradeoffs: Eliminates torn reads on the serving gateway at the expense of temporary staging disk headroom.

nodes.title: Cleanup Scheduler (60 s)
nodes.responsibility: Deletes local cached artifacts whose database records have transitioned to EXPIRED or BLOCKED.
nodes.tradeoffs: Decoupled cleanup prevents disk exhaustion while never blocking active downloads.

architectureDiagrams.title: Semantic Search & MCP Integration
architectureDiagrams.label: Messenger archive: MTProto sync service in Rust, PostgreSQL queue, Python Whisper worker, batched Rust indexer, Qdrant vector DB, and MCP server
architectureDiagrams.summary: Cross-language personal ingestion pipeline bridging PostgreSQL and Qdrant with idempotent UUIDv5 upserts and MCP tool exposure.

nodes.title: Messenger API (MTProto)
nodes.responsibility: Provides incremental message history and voice attachments subject to upstream rate limits.
nodes.tradeoffs: Rate-limited upstream API requires persistent cursor checkpoints to avoid costly full re-syncs.

nodes.title: Sync Service (Rust)
nodes.responsibility: Fetches history with exponential/flood-wait backoff and stores raw messages in PostgreSQL.
nodes.tradeoffs: Rust async runtime handles long-running sync sessions with predictable memory footprint.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL Store & Queue
nodes.responsibility: Stores canonical chat records and coordinates voice transcription jobs via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
nodes.tradeoffs: Using PostgreSQL for both storage and job queuing removes an extra broker dependency for single-node/personal scale.

nodes.title: Transcription Worker (Python)
nodes.responsibility: Claims un-transcribed voice attachments and writes transcripts back to PostgreSQL.
nodes.tradeoffs: Separating Python ML execution keeps the core Rust sync and indexing paths lightweight.

nodes.title: Batch Indexer (Rust)
nodes.responsibility: Generates local text embeddings in batches and saves the indexing cursor only after upsert confirmation.
nodes.tradeoffs: Checkpoint-after-upsert avoids distributed 2PC transactions across PostgreSQL and Qdrant.

nodes.title: Vector Store (Qdrant)
nodes.responsibility: Stores semantic embeddings keyed by deterministic UUIDv5 identifiers derived from message identity.
nodes.tradeoffs: Deterministic IDs make replay after crash completely safe without duplicate vector entries.

nodes.title: MCP Server (stdio / HTTP)
nodes.responsibility: Exposes semantic search and thread retrieval tools to LLM assistants over Model Context Protocol.
nodes.tradeoffs: Read-only query tools isolate LLM agents from direct database or MTProto credentials.

engineeringConcepts.name: Idempotency
engineeringConcepts.description: Deterministic UUIDv5 vector point IDs and safe job-claim retries ensure replaying a failed batch updates existing state rather than duplicating records.

engineeringConcepts.name: Eventual Consistency
engineeringConcepts.description: Checkpoints advance only after downstream upserts succeed, and scheduled housekeeping converges database lifecycle states with local file caches.

engineeringConcepts.name: Message Delivery Guarantees
engineeringConcepts.description: Bounded AMQP worker pools and explicit requeue paths preserve at-least-once processing guarantees across asynchronous integration stages.

engineeringConcepts.name: Failure Handling
engineeringConcepts.description: Dedicated error pipelines emit diagnostic notifications and requeue failed messages, while sync workers apply flood-wait backoff and bounded retries.

engineeringConcepts.name: Distributed Coordination
engineeringConcepts.description: PostgreSQL lifecycle tables, SKIP LOCKED job claiming, and independent 15 s / 60 s schedulers coordinate concurrent work without request-path locks.

engineeringConcepts.name: Cache Consistency
engineeringConcepts.description: Atomic move-after-download prevents partial reads, while housekeeping and cleanup jobs keep local files aligned with link expiration.

engineeringConcepts.name: Observability
engineeringConcepts.description: Structured failure alerts, explicit lifecycle state enums, and automated SonarQube quality-gate checks keep failures visible and diagnosable.

engineeringConcepts.name: Security
engineeringConcepts.description: AES-GCM authenticated encryption protects time-limited document tokens, while isolated plugin classloaders and read-only MCP boundaries limit blast radius.
